name: Aetherius AI
tag: One control screen to launch, watch and steer autonomous agent workflows as they run.

scenarios.title: Watch an invoice-processing run
scenarios.ask: Run the invoice workflow on {invoices} invoices with {workers} worker agents and show me live progress.
steps: Launcher
Started {workers} worker agents and split the batch into lots of about {=ceil(invoices / workers)}.
Telemetry
Streaming throughput, error rate and cost per invoice to the 3D flow view.
Extractor agents
Read vendor, amount and due date. Average {=round(4 + 30 / workers, 1)} seconds per invoice including queue time.
Exception lane
Moved {=ceil(invoices * 0.03)} invoices with missing PO numbers to a human queue, shown as an amber branch.
Controller
Run complete. Telemetry saved for replay.
followups: Can I pause a run midway?
Yes. Pause holds every agent after its current item. You can change a setting, like the exception rule, and resume without losing work.
It shows each agent as a node and each handoff as a flow, so a stalled step or a growing queue is visible at a glance instead of buried in logs.

scenarios.title: Catch a runaway agent
scenarios.ask: Alert me when any of our {agents} agents loops or spends more than ${budget} in an hour.
steps: Telemetry
Tracked calls, tokens and spend for {agents} agents in one-minute windows.
Loop detector
Flagged the Pricing agent: the same tool call 14 times in 3 minutes with the same input.
Guard
Paused it at ${=round(budget * 0.6, 2)} spent, before the ${budget} limit.
Notifier
Sent an alert with the last 10 steps so the owner can see where it got stuck.
followups: Will it pause agents that are just busy?
It looks for repeats with the same input, not volume. A busy agent making varied calls is not paused, only rate-limited if it hits the spend cap.
The agent's owner or an admin, from the same screen. The restart is logged with a note.

scenarios.title: Compare two workflow versions
scenarios.ask: Run version A and version B of our lead-scoring workflow on {leads} leads and compare.
steps: Launcher
Ran both versions on the same {leads} leads in parallel.
Telemetry
Recorded time, cost and score for every lead in both runs.
Comparator
Version B added {steps_b} steps. It agreed with sales-qualified outcomes {=min(12, steps_b * 3)} points more often.
Reporter
Built a side-by-side view with the 20 leads where the versions disagreed most.
followups: Both versions see the exact same leads in the same order, so the difference comes from the workflow, not the data.
Can we roll out B to part of traffic first?
Yes. Send a share of live leads to B, watch the same telemetry, and promote it when you are satisfied.
